comparator.sourceNotes: The Theatre Studies pathway closes 60+60+60 as 126 EC required, 12 EC restricted choice and 42 EC genuine free profiling. The restricted choices are instantiated as Focus op vrouwen (6 EC) in year two and Kunsteducatie (6 EC) in year three; the intervening 12-EC Dance Developments option is not cut in half. Focus requires the propedeuse while its history background is advisory; Kunsteducatie requires a positive BSA; the thesis requires the first year and compulsory second year. Diagnostic and tutoring formation are zero-credit. Current evidence supports Dutch and English instruction. Optional internship remains within genuine free space.

programmes.label: Theatre Studies (Theaterwetenschap) at University of Amsterdam

exception.reason: Three independently organised directions were tested. Theatre history, dramatic texts and dramaturgy has genuine general literary interpretation and isolated encounters with drama, Shakespeare and theatrical storytelling, but UCR offers no theatre-history sequence, dramaturgy, dramatic-text progression or theatre-specific archival research. Live performance, meaning and contemporary performance culture has one course that studies poetic performance, voice and embodiment and several film/media methods, but no live-performance analysis, spectatorship, scenography, dance studies, musical-theatre study, performance documentation or comparative performance traditions. Theatre, society, institutions and education has relevant sociology, politics, arts, heritage and communication frameworks, but no theatre institutions, theatre-and-politics sequence, arts education or theatre for young audiences. In every direction, extending adjacent material to 23 non-PPD courses would change the object of study to literature, film/media, communication or general cultural studies. The missing theatre content and methods are academic substance rather than professional qualification, so no complete UCR response is claimed.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows in the current enriched UCR workbook, including descriptions or outline-derived profiles, prerequisites and Fall-2026-start availability. MCCCOMM312 Creative Communication Laboratory directly studies poetic performance, voice, sound and embodiment, but explicitly does not provide singing, songwriting or music performance and is not a theatre/performance-studies sequence. MCCLITR111 includes drama as one literary genre; MCCLITR112 notes literature's influence on theatre; MCCLITR211 considers theatrical performance as one storytelling form; and MCCLITR311 analyses adaptation from literary texts and dramas to film, including acting. BENLEAD112 uses Shakespearean drama to study leadership rather than theatre. MCCMEDI111/112/211/311/312 provide film, media, representation and production methods, while MCCHEAM111/112/211/312/315/316 provide art, archaeology, heritage and museum study. None teaches dramaturgy, live-performance analysis, theatre history, dance or musical theatre, spectatorship, staging and scenography, theatre institutions, performance documentation, arts education or theatre-specific archival and independent research. These isolated dramatic and performative elements cannot anchor a coherent 24-course Theatre Studies response.

candidateAssessment.concept: Theatre history, dramatic texts and dramaturgy
candidateAssessment.assessment: Literary studies offers close reading, genre analysis and limited engagement with drama, while history and qualitative research offer transferable methods. UCR has no theatre-history sequence, dramaturgy, sustained dramatic-text analysis, theatre criticism, theatre-specific source criticism or archival research. General literary and historical methods cannot provide the disciplinary progression that organises this direction.

candidateAssessment.concept: Live performance, meaning and contemporary performance culture
candidateAssessment.assessment: Creative Communication Laboratory provides real study and practice of poetic performance, voice and embodiment, and film/media courses analyse mediated performance and adaptation. UCR nevertheless lacks live-performance analysis, performance theory, spectatorship, staging and scenography, dance studies, musical-theatre study, comparative performance traditions and performance documentation. Expanding film, literature and communication courses would change the object of study.

Sociology, political theory, communication, art history, heritage and media offer relevant approaches to culture and public life. Their documented content does not study theatre as a social practice, theatre institutions, theatre and politics, theatre education or theatre for young audiences. A complete curriculum would become general cultural sociology or arts and media studies.
